subject.title: fix(gateway): reject invalid session history limit with 400 instead of coercing to 1

question: Should the shipped direct session-history endpoint intentionally change malformed `limit` requests from HTTP 200 with coerced data to HTTP 400?
rationale: The patch changes an established HTTP response contract, and repository policy treats fail-closed validation and removed fallback behavior as upgrade-sensitive even when stricter behavior is desirable.

options.title: Adopt strict HTTP 400
options.body: Confirm the breaking validation contract, require safe-integer coverage and real request/response proof, then document the behavior for direct HTTP clients.

options.title: Preserve shipped coercion
options.body: Keep the existing response contract and narrow this PR to diagnostics or tests unless a later versioned API change is approved.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict HTTP 400
recommendation.body: Confirm the breaking validation contract, require safe-integer coverage and real request/response proof, then document the behavior for direct HTTP clients.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history directly owns the route implementation and HTTP authorization contract.
